subject: Discovery Recap: Migration off OpenAI/Anthropic - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@acme-corp.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: Migration off OpenAI/Anthropic - Acme Corp

Hi Jenna and Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand where Acme is with LLM usage and what success looks like. Below is a short recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of pain points
- Cost and vendor lock: heavy spend on OpenAI/Anthropic APIs and limited control over latency/cost.
- Rate limits and throttling during peak usage (real-time chat flows + async batch embeddings).
- Auditability and data governance for user PII and retention.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Generation/chat: OpenAI Chat API (gpt-4.1 / gpt-4o) for product recommendations and support completions.
- Embeddings: Anthropic embeddings for search/semantic match (batched nightly).
- Orchestration: Node.js microservices + Redis cache + Kubernetes.
- Monitoring: Datadog + custom logging, but limited token-level cost visibility.

Success criteria (what would make this migration successful)
1) Maintain or improve latency for 95th percentile chat flows (<200ms added tail).
2) Reduce per-token inference spend by >=40% while preserving model quality for main prompts.
3) Seamless compatibility with current request semantics (chat + embeddings) and minimal application code changes.
4) Auditability: model and request logs retained for 90 days and accessible for compliance.

Initial shortlist & compatibility notes
- Llama 2 (70B) / fine-tuned chat variant — good for chat quality and widely supported.
- Mistral-Chat or Mistral-Instruct (convincing chat quality at lower cost).
- Falcon-40B-Instruct or RedPajama-Chat for cheaper embeddings and generation trade-offs.
- Evaluate quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) for cost-sensitive pools.

Technical compatibility considerations
- We understand you use streaming chat responses and embeddings API with batched jobs; Redwood can expose the same REST/SDK interface and map requests to model families.
- We recommend a canary approach: internal traffic -> pilot model variant -> A/B compare quality and latency.

Attachments: redwood-migration-plan.pdf, model-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (high-level mapping).

Next steps (proposed)
1) Technical deep dive with your infra/ML engineers (Dev + 60m) — please propose times.
2) Provide a short sample of representative prompts & embedding vectors (we can sign an NDA if needed).
3) Redwood to deliver an initial TCO estimate + rollout plan within 5 business days after the deep dive.

If that sounds right I can coordinate calendars — copying Dev and Logan to pick the deep-dive slot.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the data, Jenna — that file is super helpful. High-level technical notes before the deep dive:

1) Embeddings dimensionality
- Anthropic embeddings you currently use are ~1536 dims (per your note). Many open embedding models vary (1024/1536/4096). Redwood can normalize by providing a model-compatibility layer: we can (a) surface model native dims, and (b) optionally store/serve fixed-dim vectors via an up/down-projection step to keep your similarity pipeline stable.

2) Streaming/chat parity
- Streaming semantics (token-by-token flush) are supported for all shortlisted chat models; Redwood will preserve the same request/response streaming APIs so minimal client changes.

3) Shortlist rationale + expected trade-offs
- Llama 2 (70B, chat-tuned): best overall fidelity to your current prompts; larger memory needs but excellent for quality-critical flows.
- Mistral-Chat / Mistral-Instruct: strong instruction-following at lower cost — good for mid-tier to high-throughput endpoints.
- Falcon/RedPajama (40B family): good cost-to-quality for embedding-heavy or lower-F1 generation use cases.
- Quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) can cut GPU cost by ~2–3x at modest quality degradation; we recommend A/B testing on key prompts.

4) Integration work & timelines
- Pilot plan (4–6 weeks): 1 week infra setup & model selection; 2–3 weeks A/B + quality evals; 1 week rollout & cutover testing. This aligns with your mid-April pilot target if we start early March.

5) Compliance / attestations
- Redwood provides SOC 2 Type II report, encryption at rest/transit, and audit logs. We’ll attach the certs in the next email.

Next actions I’ll take:
- Prep a short tech agenda for the deep dive and share a calendar invite for Wed/Thu next week per Jenna’s availability.
- Spin up a small demo environment with Llama-2-70B and Mistral-Chat variants and share perf numbers (latency / tokens / cost) for your representative prompts.

If that works I’ll schedule the deep dive and share the invite.
